posts.raw_content:
Like many of you I knew the history of Russia/Ukraine stretched back generations but  was certainly no expert on it.  Asked Gemini for some assistance.  It follows>

>The roots of the ethnic, political, and historical tension between Ukraine and Russia go back roughly 1,000 years, rooted in a shared origin point that both nations claim. However, the concept of a distinct ethnic and national identity conflict—often called an "ethno-war"—developed in key evolutionary stages over the centuries.   


>1. Shared Roots and Divergence (9th–13th Centuries)Kievan Rus (c. 882–1240): Both Ukrainians and Russians trace their cultural and political heritage back to Kievan Rus, a medieval federation centered in Kyiv.   The Mongol Fragmentation (1237–1240): When the Mongol invasion destroyed Kievan Rus, the East Slavic lands fragmented along distinct cultural and political lines:   The North-East: Became dominated by the Grand Duchy of Moscow (Muscovy), which evolved into the Tsardom of Russia.   The West and South: Territories comprising modern Ukraine were absorbed into the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. Centuries of exposure to Western European political and linguistic influences fostered a distinct Ukrainian language and culture.


>2. Cossack Era and Tsarist Imperial Rule (17th–19th Centuries)
Pereyaslav Agreement (1654): To gain protection against Polish forces, Ukrainian Cossack leader Bohdan Khmelnytsky signed an alliance with Tsar Alexis of Russia. Moscow interpreted this as an irreversible annexation, whereas Ukrainian leaders saw it as a temporary military alliance.

>Imperial Suppression: As the Russian Empire expanded, it enacted aggressive Russification policies aiming to erase a distinct Ukrainian ethnic identity:

>Valuev Circular (1863) & Ems Ukaz (1876): Bans were placed on printing books, publishing literature, or delivering school instruction in the Ukrainian language, which the imperial government dismissed as merely a "Little Russian" dialect.


>3. Revolutionary Period & Early Soviet Eras (1917–1930s)Ukrainian War of Independence (1917–1921): Following the fall of the Russian Tsar, Ukrainians declared the independent Ukrainian People's Republic. Bolshevik Red forces invaded, leading to years of military conflict until Ukraine was forcibly integrated into the USSR as the Ukrainian SSR.The Holodomor (1932–1933): Under Joseph Stalin's regime, forced agricultural collectivization caused a man-made famine in Ukraine that killed millions. Widely recognized as genocide, this event cemented severe historical trauma and deep-seated anti-Moscow hostility across generations.   


>4. Modern Russo-Ukrainian War (2014–Present)Following the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, Ukraine voted overwhelmingly for independence. Modern armed conflict broke out in 2014 after the Euromaidan protests, leading to Russia's annexation of Crimea and military support for separatists in Donbas, escalating into a full-scale invasion in February 2022.   


Throw in the Bush II admin's push to incorporate Ukraine into NATO,  and here we are.  Couple that w/ the shenanigans that occurred under Obama and Biden and of course it is far worse.
